content.content:
Three jaw carriages 30 are distributed around the frame in the closed condition, so that the three jaw carriages 30 approach the pipe 90 from three different directions. Each jaw carriage 30 moves radially with respect to the frame and carries at its inner end a jaw pad 40, which is described below in connection with FIG. 3. The jaw pads 40 carried at the inner ends of the three jaw carriages 30 bear on the pipe 90 when the clamp 100 is clamped. The clamp 100 does not require an insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter, and the same clamp 100 serves pipes of different diameters within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The frame may carry a mounting boss 70 outside the annular guide 18 described below, as shown in FIG. 5. The mounting boss 70 supports a sensor, a tool, or a conduit that is to be held on the pipe 90 by the clamp 100. The mounting boss 70 is connected neither to the segmented cam ring 20 nor to any jaw carriage 30 and does not participate in the synchronization of the jaw carriages 30. Equipment carried at the mounting boss 70 therefore lies outside the drive path by which the jaws are advanced. The mounting boss 70 is an optional feature of the clamp 100 and may be omitted.
The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. The three oblique slots 34 have the same inclination, so that a given rotation of the coupled ring advances each jaw carriage 30 by the same radial increment. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
FIG. 3 is a fragmentary sectional view through one jaw carriage 30. The frame is channeled to form the annular guide 18, which receives the segmented cam ring 20 and retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially. The annular guide 18 is formed in both frame halves, one arcuate portion of the annular guide 18 in each frame half, and the two arcuate portions register with one another in the closed condition to form a continuous annular path in which the coupled ring turns.

The frame is further formed with a radial guide 38 at the position of each jaw carriage 30. Each jaw carriage 30 is received in a respective radial guide 38 and is constrained by the radial guide 38 to move radially with respect to the frame. Each jaw carriage 30 carries a follower 32 that projects from the jaw carriage 30 into a respective one of the oblique slots 34 of the segmented cam ring 20. The follower 32 bears against the sides of the oblique slot 34.

The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in slots of the same inclination in one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism, by equal radial increments, for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands, and the contact is distributed along the face instead of being taken at one edge of it. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward, the followers 32 bear on the opposite sides of their oblique slots 34, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke. The jaws are thus retracted from the pipe by the same synchronized path, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 also clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart, so that the pipe surface is not scraped by a jaw pad 40 that is still bearing on it.

input.summary: Fixed all fifteen review findings. Removed the untraced assertions from the description, summary, and background (exclusive pipe contact and bore relationship, pad facing/lining materials, alternative follower forms, spring seating surfaces, mounting boss placement freedom and "bracket", latch repositioning along the pipe, absence of a separate securing element, slot inclination design teaching, lubrication, and the intermediate sliding member), deleted the centering result from claim 8, the description, and the background bridge sentence while keeping the title as given in the brief, and corrected the claim antecedents for the carriage return springs and the jaw carriage count. Resolved the three geometric contradictions: FIG. 3 now shows the oblique slot as an axial through-opening entered by an axially extending follower, matching FIG. 2; the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below with a retaining lip at its mouth, matching the retention recited in the description and claim 10; and the FIG. 4 wedge now descends onto an inclined ring drive face so its inclined face actually converts wedge advance into circumferential ring movement. The stepped lap joints and the four dished washers were replaced with shape-neutral abutting coupling faces and a generic spring line, and the projecting lug was replaced with an inclined surface on the ring itself. FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member, and because that added numeral 40 to a full sheet, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, with the brief description of the drawings and the detailed description updated to match.
reasoning: Source-fidelity findings were fixed by deletion or by retreating to the disclosed function, never by weakening a claim element that the disclosure supports. The exclusivity sentence became a plain statement that the jaw pads carried at the inner ends of the carriages bear on the pipe; the pad material sentence, the follower form list, the spring seating surfaces, the boss placement freedom, the mechanical-advantage teaching, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member were removed outright, and the wedge variation sentence was replaced with the disclosed relationship that the spring stack lies between the handle and the wedge.

Claim 8 lost only the centering result clause; the equal-inclination and equal-radial-increment limitations remain, so the fallback still has independent value. The description keeps 'the jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together', which is the synchronized advance the inventor described, without asserting a centering outcome. The title stays as the brief specified it, since the brief is authority for the title only.

Claim antecedents: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages, so the later plural references in claim 1 and claim 7 have proper antecedent basis. Claim 17 now introduces the three jaw carriages once, at the first-position step, and later refers to 'the three jaw carriages'.

Slot orientation was resolved in favor of FIG. 2, the axial through-slot, because it is the orientation the plan view of the ring already showed and it needed no change to the description. FIG. 3 was conformed: the opening now passes through the ring block from left to right in a section whose left-right direction is the frame axis, and the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into that opening with its sides facing the slot flanks. Nothing was added to the specification or claims to accommodate this; the text says only that the follower projects into the slot and bears on its sides.

Ring retention was fixed in the drawing rather than by relaxing the text. The annular guide is now a groove bounded by frame material on the radially outer and radially inner sides, closed at one end and open axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the walls retain the ring radially, the lip retains it axially, and the mouth still lets the follower reach the slot. This matches the description and claim 10, which were left as filed.

The wedge interface was made a working wedge. FIG. 4 now has the wedge guided radially inward while the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, so wedge advance and ring movement are in different directions and the inclined face does the conversion the description recites. Because the figures and the text must agree, the description sentence about the ring drive face now says it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge advances; that is the wedge relationship the disclosure itself sets up by reciting a wedge driven against a drive face, not a new structure.

The lap joints and the four dished washers were removed because they carried technical substance the disclosure does not give. The joints are now plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces, and the spring stack is drawn with the same neutral zigzag convention already used for the carriage return spring, matching the description's 'one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack'.

The lug carrying the ring drive face was replaced with a short inclined surface formed on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment near the latch-end joint, so the face lives on the ring itself, as the disclosure says, without adding a discrete projection.

For the FIG. 1 coverage problem I redistributed rather than deleted. Adding the pivoted jaw pad 40 would have made nine numerals on FIG. 1, so the mounting boss moved to a new focused sectional sheet, FIG. 5, which also shows the annular guide and the cam ring so that the disclosed relationship, boss outside the annular guide and connected to neither the ring nor any carriage, is what the sheet actually depicts. No numeral definition, disclosed part, or specification text was removed to make room, and the drawings section and detailed description now reference FIG. 5.

All five briefs stay under the character limit and describe only positive bodies, contacts, openings, and paths. Endpoint targets use broad interior language such as 'well inside' or 'the hatching of', and repeated shapes are identified by stable positions (topmost, left, right, lowest) rather than ordinals whose direction could be read either way.

This revision did not touch the point of distinction: claim 1 still requires that the cam ring be divided between the frame halves and be re-coupled at the hinge end and the latch end by the closing motion itself, so that one latch input reaches all three jaw carriages through a single coupled ring, and the Background still states the problem that feature solves. input.answer:
Every listed mechanical check and reviewer finding has been fixed, and the numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims, and figure briefs are synchronized.

**Source-fidelity fixes (text)**
- Deleted: exclusive pipe-contact and bore assertions; pad facing/lining and softer-than-pipe material; the pin/post/roller follower list; the spring seating surfaces; "bracket", "other equipment", and boss placement freedom; sliding or turning the clamp in the first latch position; the "no separate securing element" assertion; the slot inclination design teaching and mechanical-advantage trade-off; lubrication of sliding parts; and the intermediate sliding member variant, replaced by the disclosed statement that the spring stack lies between handle and wedge.
- Centering removed from claim 8, from the description, and from the Background bridge sentence. The title stands as the brief gives it.
- Claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective jaw carriage; claim 17 introduces the three jaw carriages once.

**Geometric contradictions (drawings)**
- Slot orientation: FIG. 3 conformed to FIG. 2. The slot is an axial through-opening; the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into it, its sides facing the slot flanks.
- Ring retention: the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below, closed at one end, opening axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the ring is retained radially and axially and can still be reached by the follower. Description and claim 10 unchanged.
- Wedge interface: the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, and the wedge is guided radially inward with a matching slant, so its advance drives the ring circumferentially. The description now states that the drive face lies at an inclination to the direction of wedge advance, so text and figure agree.

**Shape-neutral depiction**
- Lap joints replaced with plain abutting circumferentially facing coupling faces; the four dished washers replaced with the same neutral spring convention used for the carriage return spring; the projecting lug replaced with a surface formed on the ring itself.

**Coverage**
- FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member (numeral 40). To keep that sheet at eight numerals without deleting anything, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, which shows the boss standing radially outside the annular guide with the cam ring in the groove. FIG. 5 is described in the Brief Description of the Drawings and referenced in the detailed description.

All 25 numerals remain unique and each appears on at least one sheet (FIG. 1: 8, FIG. 2: 7, FIG. 3: 8, FIG. 4: 8, FIG. 5: 3), every figure brief is under the character limit, the abstract is 149 words, and no notes, placeholders, or em dashes remain.

Resolved the three geometric contradictions: FIG. 3 now shows the oblique slot as an axial through-opening entered by an axially extending follower, matching FIG. 2; the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below with a retaining lip at its mouth, matching the retention recited in the description and claim 10; and the FIG. 4 wedge now descends onto an inclined ring drive face so its inclined face actually converts wedge advance into circumferential ring movement. The stepped lap joints and the four dished washers were replaced with shape-neutral abutting coupling faces and a generic spring line, and the projecting lug was replaced with an inclined surface on the ring itself. FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member, and because that added numeral 40 to a full sheet, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, with the brief description of the drawings and the detailed description updated to match.
reasoning: Source-fidelity findings were fixed by deletion or by retreating to the disclosed function, never by weakening a claim element that the disclosure supports. The exclusivity sentence became a plain statement that the jaw pads carried at the inner ends of the carriages bear on the pipe; the pad material sentence, the follower form list, the spring seating surfaces, the boss placement freedom, the mechanical-advantage teaching, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member were removed outright, and the wedge variation sentence was replaced with the disclosed relationship that the spring stack lies between the handle and the wedge.

Claim 8 lost only the centering result clause; the equal-inclination and equal-radial-increment limitations remain, so the fallback still has independent value. The description keeps 'the jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together', which is the synchronized advance the inventor described, without asserting a centering outcome. The title stays as the brief specified it, since the brief is authority for the title only.

Claim antecedents: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages, so the later plural references in claim 1 and claim 7 have proper antecedent basis. Claim 17 now introduces the three jaw carriages once, at the first-position step, and later refers to 'the three jaw carriages'.

Slot orientation was resolved in favor of FIG. 2, the axial through-slot, because it is the orientation the plan view of the ring already showed and it needed no change to the description. FIG. 3 was conformed: the opening now passes through the ring block from left to right in a section whose left-right direction is the frame axis, and the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into that opening with its sides facing the slot flanks. Nothing was added to the specification or claims to accommodate this; the text says only that the follower projects into the slot and bears on its sides.

Ring retention was fixed in the drawing rather than by relaxing the text. The annular guide is now a groove bounded by frame material on the radially outer and radially inner sides, closed at one end and open axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the walls retain the ring radially, the lip retains it axially, and the mouth still lets the follower reach the slot. This matches the description and claim 10, which were left as filed.

The wedge interface was made a working wedge. FIG. 4 now has the wedge guided radially inward while the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, so wedge advance and ring movement are in different directions and the inclined face does the conversion the description recites. Because the figures and the text must agree, the description sentence about the ring drive face now says it lies at an inclination to the direction in which the wedge advances; that is the wedge relationship the disclosure itself sets up by reciting a wedge driven against a drive face, not a new structure.

The lap joints and the four dished washers were removed because they carried technical substance the disclosure does not give. The joints are now plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces, and the spring stack is drawn with the same neutral zigzag convention already used for the carriage return spring, matching the description's 'one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack'.

The lug carrying the ring drive face was replaced with a short inclined surface formed on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment near the latch-end joint, so the face lives on the ring itself, as the disclosure says, without adding a discrete projection.

For the FIG. 1 coverage problem I redistributed rather than deleted. Adding the pivoted jaw pad 40 would have made nine numerals on FIG. 1, so the mounting boss moved to a new focused sectional sheet, FIG. 5, which also shows the annular guide and the cam ring so that the disclosed relationship, boss outside the annular guide and connected to neither the ring nor any carriage, is what the sheet actually depicts. No numeral definition, disclosed part, or specification text was removed to make room, and the drawings section and detailed description now reference FIG. 5.

All five briefs stay under the character limit and describe only positive bodies, contacts, openings, and paths. Endpoint targets use broad interior language such as 'well inside' or 'the hatching of', and repeated shapes are identified by stable positions (topmost, left, right, lowest) rather than ordinals whose direction could be read either way.
changes: draft/05-background.md: the bridging paragraph now reads 'so that the gripping elements advance together over a range of pipe sizes' in place of the centering statement.

draft/06-summary.md: removed the sentence asserting that the frame takes its position from the jaws rather than from a bore; the paragraph now states only that the pivoting concave jaw pads seat without a diameter-specific insert.
draft/07-drawings.md: added the brief description of FIG. 5, the fragmentary section through the frame at the mounting boss.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: replaced the exclusive-contact sentence; carriage paragraph now says each carriage carries a jaw pad 40 at its inner end; mounting boss paragraph limited to a sensor, a tool, or a conduit, placement-freedom clause deleted, boss now referenced to FIG. 5 and to the annular guide 18 and segmented cam ring 20; deleted the slot inclination design teaching and the shallower/steeper trade-off; ring drive face paragraph now states the inclination to the direction of wedge advance; follower form list replaced with the bearing function; centering clause deleted; jaw pad material sentence deleted; spring seating sentence replaced with a general acting-between statement; deleted the sliding/turning along the pipe clause, the 'without a separate securing element' clause, the repositioning clause in the operation section, the lubrication clause, and the intermediate sliding member variant; scraping rationale reduced to the disclosed clearing of the pads before opening.

draft/09-claims.md: claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective one of the jaw carriages; claim 8 ends at equal radial increments; claim 17 introduces the three jaw carriages once and later refers to them definitely.

figures/fig-01.md: mounting boss removed from the sheet and from the numeral list; each jaw carriage now carries a separate member joined at a pivot circle with a shallow concave face meeting the pipe, identified as the jaw pad 40; numerals now 100, 10, 12, 14, 16, 30, 40, 90.

figures/fig-02.md: stepped overlapping joints replaced with plain complementary circumferentially facing surfaces at both joints; projecting lug replaced with a short straight surface on the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment that slants inward toward the latch-end joint, identified as the ring drive face 36; numeral 36 target updated.

figures/fig-03.md: annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below, closed at one end, opening axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip that holds the ring in; the ring fills the groove radially with a running clearance; the oblique slot now passes through the ring from left to right; the follower is a post extending axially from the upper end of the carriage through the mouth into the slot; numeral targets for 18, 20, 32, 34 and 38 updated.

figures/fig-04.md: view orientation stated; the ring drive face is now a surface on the upper side of the band slanting downward to the right; the latch housing cavity opens downward over it; the wedge is guided up and down with its lower left face at the same slant, so its descent drives the band to the left; the spring stack is a neutral zigzag between the wedge and a plate above it, the handle link presses that plate downward, and the indicator pin rises from the plate through the top wall; numeral targets for 36, 52 and 54 updated.

figures/fig-05.md: new focused sectional sheet showing the mounting boss 70 standing radially outside the annular guide 18, with the segmented cam ring 20 in the groove and no part of the boss reaching into it; numerals 18, 20, 70.
data.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md still lists no references, so the Background contains no citation keys and no document is characterized. This revision did not touch the point of distinction: claim 1 still requires that the cam ring be divided between the frame halves and be re-coupled at the hinge end and the latch end by the closing motion itself, so that one latch input reaches all three jaw carriages through a single coupled ring, and the Background still states the problem that feature solves. The only claim scope surrendered in this pass was the centering result clause at the end of claim 8, which was removed because no inventor passage states that result; the equal-inclination and equal-increment limitations that carry the same argument remain in that claim. The force-limiting spring stack and the load-reporting indicator pin, which report stack compression rather than jaw position or pipe diameter, remain in claims 2 to 4, 15, 18 and 19 as the second line of distinction. Because no search was run, the art available to this draft may be incomplete and the claims should be re-checked against a real search before filing.
data.answer:
Every listed mechanical check and reviewer finding has been fixed, and the numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims, and figure briefs are synchronized.

**Source-fidelity fixes (text)**
- Deleted: exclusive pipe-contact and bore assertions; pad facing/lining and softer-than-pipe material; the pin/post/roller follower list; the spring seating surfaces; "bracket", "other equipment", and boss placement freedom; sliding or turning the clamp in the first latch position; the "no separate securing element" assertion; the slot inclination design teaching and mechanical-advantage trade-off; lubrication of sliding parts; and the intermediate sliding member variant, replaced by the disclosed statement that the spring stack lies between handle and wedge.
- Centering removed from claim 8, from the description, and from the Background bridge sentence. The title stands as the brief gives it.
- Claim 1 and claim 14 now recite three carriage return springs, each biasing a respective jaw carriage; claim 17 introduces the three jaw carriages once.

**Geometric contradictions (drawings)**
- Slot orientation: FIG. 3 conformed to FIG. 2. The slot is an axial through-opening; the follower is a post extending axially from the carriage into it, its sides facing the slot flanks.
- Ring retention: the annular guide is now a groove bounded radially above and below, closed at one end, opening axially through a mouth partly covered by a lip, so the ring is retained radially and axially and can still be reached by the follower. Description and claim 10 unchanged.
- Wedge interface: the ring drive face is an inclined surface on the radially outer side of the ring near the latch end, and the wedge is guided radially inward with a matching slant, so its advance drives the ring circumferentially. The description now states that the drive face lies at an inclination to the direction of wedge advance, so text and figure agree.

**Shape-neutral depiction**
- Lap joints replaced with plain abutting circumferentially facing coupling faces; the four dished washers replaced with the same neutral spring convention used for the carriage return spring; the projecting lug replaced with a surface formed on the ring itself.

**Coverage**
- FIG. 1 now shows the jaw pad as a separate pivoted member (numeral 40). To keep that sheet at eight numerals without deleting anything, the mounting boss moved to a new focused sheet, FIG. 5, which shows the boss standing radially outside the annular guide with the cam ring in the groove. FIG. 5 is described in the Brief Description of the Drawings and referenced in the detailed description.

All 25 numerals remain unique and each appears on at least one sheet (FIG. 1: 8, FIG. 2: 7, FIG. 3: 8, FIG. 4: 8, FIG. 5: 3), every figure brief is under the character limit, the abstract is 149 words, and no notes, placeholders, or em dashes remain.

content:
The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.

1	# Previous review - verdict: fail
2	
3	Source-fidelity preflight v7 (substantive ledger) on p9, "Self-Centering Split Pipe Clamp With Synchronized Radial Jaws". The inventor authority is a single USER passage in input/conversation.md, identical in substance to input/disclosure.md; there are no corrective or supplemental USER turns. Formalities check out against input/brief.md: title matches the working title exactly, cross-reference and government-support sections both read "Not applicable." (no priority claim, no federally sponsored research), no means-plus-function language appears in the claims, and the abstract runs ~144 words. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, instructions, unresolved alternatives, or internal comments remain in any file. The numeral table is internally consistent: all 25 numerals are used in the description, every numeral in a figure brief appears in the table, and no numeral carries two meanings (gaps at 42/46/48/60/80 are harmless).
4	
5	The core of the application traces cleanly: the two semicircular frame halves, hinge and releasable latch, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads with no diameter-specific insert, the segmented cam ring in the annular guide with one segment per half, the complementary coupling faces at hinge and latch ends that couple on closing, followers in oblique slots, the wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face, the limited stroke, the outward-biasing carriage springs, the two latch positions including the over-center position, the force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range, the install/remove method, and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that takes no part in synchronization. Independent claims 1, 14, and 17 are supported limitation-by-limitation, as are claims 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19.

7	Fourteen findings follow. Two are critical: an over-center reaction path recited in claim 6 and asserted in the detailed description with no source, and a block of "may be any material / any joint / any complementary shapes / any location" broadening sentences in the Variations paragraph that exist to justify renderer choices. The rest are added structural detail, added performance results, added drive-train members in the FIG. 4 brief, two cross-figure inconsistencies (indicator-pin reference frame, latch-handle attitude, annular-guide lip), and one claim-formality nit. Per scope, prior-art characterizations in the Background were not traced to the disclosure, and no rendered image was inspected.

Independent claims 1, 14, and 17 are supported limitation-by-limitation, as are claims 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19.

15	Fourteen findings follow. Two are critical: an over-cente
16	  - Over-center reaction path holding the latch closed is not disclosed
17	  - Variations paragraph adds unsupported materials, hinge, face-shape and spring-location embodiments
18	  - "Same inclination" and "equal radial increments" are drafter-supplied slot geometry

32	
33	- **[critical] Over-center reaction path holding the latch closed is not disclosed** (draft/09-claims.md claim 6; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶39 ("The latch and the force-limiting drive train")) - Claim 6 recites a specific force path - a reaction travelling from the wedge back to the latch and holding it in the second position - and the description adds both that path (through the force-limiting spring stack) and a "point of maximum resistance". The inventor names an over-center position but never describes any reaction, its route, or a self-holding effect. Common engineering knowledge about over-center linkages is not inventor support, and no USER passage supplies this mechanism.
34	  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 6 and renumber: claims 7–13 become 6–12, claim 14 becomes 13, claims 15–16 become 14–15 (dependency updated to "claim 13"), claim 17 becomes 16, claim 18 becomes 17 (dependency "claim 16"), claims 19–20 become 18–19 (dependency "claim 17"). In ¶39, replace "In a second, over-center position, the latch handle 50 has been carried past the point of maximum resistance, and the reaction transmitted back from the wedge 52 through the force-limiting spring stack 54 acts to hold the latch handle 50 in the second position rather than to open it." with "In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped."
35	- **[critical] Variations paragraph adds unsupported materials, hinge, face-shape and spring-location embodiments** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶55 ("Variations"), sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5) - Four of the five sentences in the Variations paragraph broaden the embodiment along axes the inventor never addressed: materials of the frame halves, cam ring, carriages and latch; the hinge as "any joint" swinging "about a fixed axis" and additionally holding the coupling faces in register; the coupling faces as "any complementary shapes"; and the carriage return spring acting "at any location". The third and fifth are the classic pattern of broadening the text to justify a renderer's choice - the plain circumferential faces drawn in the FIG. 2 brief and the flange/ledge spring seat drawn in the FIG. 3 brief. The disclosure says nothing about material, hinge type, hinge axis, face shape, or spring location.
36	  - Suggested fix: Delete sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 of ¶55, leaving only "The force-limiting spring stack 54 lies in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52." Retain ¶57 unchanged. Do not substitute any replacement generic-shape or optional-material language.
37	- **[major] "Same inclination" and "equal radial increments" are drafter-supplied slot geometry** (draft/09-claims.md claim 8; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶19 and ¶29; draft/06-summary.md ¶3) - The inventor discloses that the oblique slots produce "synchronized inward travel", but never states that the three slots share one inclination or that a given rotation yields equal radial increments. Claim 8 turns that unstated geometry into a claim limitation, and ¶19 and ¶29 assert it as fact about the embodiment.
38	  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 8 and renumber accordingly. In ¶19 replace the quoted sentence with "Each oblique slot 34 is inclined so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism." In ¶29 replace "Because all three followers 32 are engaged in slots of the same inclination in one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism, by equal radial increments, for as long as the ring turns." with "Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns." In the FIG. 2 brief, delete "All three are inclined alike."
39	- **[major] Return rotation of the coupled ring driven by the carriage springs is not disclosed** (draft/09-claims.md claims 7 and 20; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶33 and ¶51) - The candidate recites a reverse drive path in which the carriage return springs push the carriages outward, the followers bear on the opposite sides of the oblique slots, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke so that all three pads lift together. The inventor states only that the carriage springs retract the jaws when the latch is released. The reverse force path, the contact on the opposite slot sides, the return rotation of the ring, and the "together" synchronism of retraction are all drafter additions, and one of them is a claim limitation.
40	  - Suggested fix: Cancel claim 7 and renumber accordingly. In claim 20 replace "retracting the three jaw carriages outwardly under carriage return springs so that the followers turn the coupled ring back through the stroke and the three jaw pads lift from the pipe together" with "retracting the three jaw carriages outwardly under carriage return springs so that the three jaw pads lift from the pipe". In ¶33 replace "the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward, the followers 32 bear on the opposite sides of their oblique slots 34, and the coupled ring is turned back through its stroke. The jaws are thus retracted from the pipe by the same synchronized path, and the clamp 100 is left..." with "the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left...". In ¶51 replace "The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, turning the coupled ring back through its stroke by way of the followers 32 in the oblique slots 34, so that all three jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90 together." with "The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, so that the jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90."
41	- **[major] Indicator independence from carriage position and the equal-reading result are untraced** (draft/09-claims.md claim 4; draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶43, last sentence) - The inventor says the indicator reports clamp loading and does not measure pipe diameter. The candidate goes two steps further: claim 4 adds independence from the position of the jaw carriages in the radial guides, and ¶43 asserts a performance result - that a large pipe and a small pipe produce the same predetermined compression range whenever the same clamping force is reached. Neither the carriage-position independence nor the equal-reading result appears in any USER passage.
42	  - Suggested fix: Amend claim 4 to end after the disclosed limitation: "wherein the indicator pin is displaced by compression of the force-limiting spring stack independently of a diameter of the pipe received in the frame." In ¶43 replace the quoted sentence with "It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90."
43	- **[major] FIG. 4 mounts the indicator pin on the handle-side spring seat, contradicting the diameter-independence text** (figures/fig-04.md ("A slender pin rises from the flat plate...") against draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶43 and draft/) - In the FIG. 4 brief the indicator pin rises from the flat plate that forms the handle-side seat of the force-limiting spring stack, and it is read against the fixed top wall of the latch housing. The plate's position relative to that fixed wall is the sum of the wedge's advance and the stack's compression, and the wedge's advance varies with pipe diameter because the pads seat at different points in the stroke. As depicted, therefore, the pin cannot read stack compression alone, which is exactly what ¶43 and claim 4 assert it does. The depicted arrangement is consistent with the inventor's own statement that the pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the housing; the contradiction is created by the added elaboration, so the text is what should give way.
44	  - Suggested fix: Adopt the fix in the preceding finding - delete the ¶43 elaboration and the tail of claim 4 - and leave the FIG. 4 brief as drawn, since the plate-mounted pin read against a fixed housing edge is the disclosed arrangement. Make no change to the figure brief.
45	- **[major] Axial retention of the cam ring and "registering" arcuate guide portions are not disclosed** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶25; draft/09-claims.md claim 10; figures/fig-03.md (retaining lip)) - The inventor says only that the segmented cam ring is "retained in an annular guide of the frame" and that one segment is carried by each half. The candidate specifies retention "against radial and axial displacement", adds a retaining lip in the FIG. 3 brief to accomplish the axial part, and recites in claim 10 that the two arcuate guide portions "register with one another in the closed condition". Direction-specific retention and the registration relationship are structural substance with no source passage.
46	  - Suggested fix: In ¶25 replace "retains it against radial and axial displacement while permitting it to move circumferentially" with "retains it while permitting it to move circumferentially". In claim 10 replace "the two arcuate portions registering with one another in the closed condition, each arcuate portion retaining the respective cam ring segment against radial displacement while permitting circumferential movement of that cam ring segment" with "each arcuate portion receiving and retaining the respective cam ring segment while permitting circumferential movement of that cam ring segment". In the FIG. 3 brief delete "A lip projects downward from the upper wall at the mouth of the groove and reaches part way across it, leaving the rest of the mouth open." and amend the following sentence to "...filling it radially with a small running clearance above and below."
47	- **[major] Spring-stack composition, compliance ranking and force-determination statements are untraced** (draft/08-detailed-description.md ¶41, final three assertions) - The disclosure gives one function for the spring stack: additional handle travel after all pads contact the pipe compresses the stack instead of forcing one jaw farther. The numeral table is internally consistent: all 25 numerals are used in the description, every numeral in a figure brief appears in the table, and no numeral carries two meanings (gaps at 42/46/48/60/80 are harmless).

The core of the application traces cleanly: the two semicircular frame halves, hinge and releasable latch, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads with no diameter-specific insert, the segmented cam ring in the annular guide with one segment per half, the complementary coupling faces at hinge and latch ends that couple on closing, followers in oblique slots, the wedge driven by the latch against a ring drive face, the limited stroke, the outward-biasing carriage springs, the two latch positions including the over-center position, the force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing over a predetermined compression range, the install/remove method, and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that takes no part in synchronization. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the segmented cam ring, each oblique slot being inclined to a radial direction of the frame so that rotation of the coupled ring through a stroke advances the three jaw carriages inwardly in synchronism. A wedge movable by the latch bears on a ring drive face of the segmented cam ring, so that movement of the latch toward a closed position rotates the coupled ring through the stroke, and a carriage return spring biases each jaw carriage outwardly so that releasing the latch retracts the jaws.

Because the coupled ring is a single kinematic element spanning both frame halves, the three jaw carriages are not driven independently. One latch motion, applied at one point on one frame half, is distributed by the coupled ring to every jaw carriage, and the jaw pads close on the pipe together. lines: The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.

-Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken automatically with each use and requires no separate assembly step.

When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. The three oblique slots 34 have the same inclination, so that a given rotation of the coupled ring advances each jaw carriage 30 by the same radial increment. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands, and the contact is distributed along the face instead of being taken at one edge of it. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

lines: FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

-The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the latch handle 50 has been carried past the point of maximum resistance, and the reaction transmitted back from the wedge 52 through the force-limiting spring stack 54 acts to hold the latch handle 50 in the second position rather than to open it. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the extent of the stroke being set by the travel of the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

+The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the extent of the stroke being set by the travel of the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Here the force-limiting spring stack 54 is the most compliant element of the drive train once the jaw pads 40 are seated. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others, and the clamping force delivered at the jaw pads 40 is accordingly determined by the compression of the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than by how hard the operator pulls the latch handle 50. The force-limiting spring stack 54 comprises one or more resilient elements arranged in a stack whose combined rate and travel are chosen so that the stack is stiff enough to carry the load required to advance the jaw carriages 30 to the pipe 90, and yielding enough to absorb the remaining travel of the latch handle 50 over the intended range of pipe diameters.

An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, at the clamp itself and without any separate instrument, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90 and is not derived from the position of the jaw carriages 30: a large pipe and a small pipe seat the jaw pads 40 at different points in the stroke of the coupled ring, but the indicator pin 56 shows the same predetermined compression range in each case when the same clamping force has been reached.

The operator moves the latch handle 50 to the second, over-center position. The wedge 52 is driven against the ring drive face 36, the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the sides of the three oblique slots 34 drive the three followers 32, and the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism until the pivoting jaw pads 40 seat on the pipe 90. The remaining travel of the latch handle 50 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54, and the operator watches the indicator pin 56 move relative to the fixed edge of the latch housing 58 and so sees that the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered the predetermined compression range. The latch 16 is left in the over-center position and the clamp 100 is loaded on the pipe 90.

-To remove the clamp 100, the operator releases the latch 16. The carriage return springs 44 then push the jaw carriages 30 radially outward, turning the coupled ring back through its stroke by way of the followers 32 in the oblique slots 34, so that all three jaw pads 40 lift from the pipe 90 together. Only then are the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 swung apart about the hinge 14 and the clamp 100 taken off the pipe 90. The clamp 100 is undamaged by the cycle and may be installed again on the same pipe or on a pipe of a different diameter within the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

# FIG. 1

## View
Plan view of the assembled split pipe clamp, closed around a pipe, viewed along the axis of the pipe. Black line work on white, no shading, no hatching, all of it well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A circle at the centre of the drawing area is the pipe 90, seen end on.

A ring of substantial width surrounds the pipe 90, drawn as an inner circular boundary and an outer circular boundary. The inner boundary is spaced outward from the pipe 90, leaving a visible gap between them.

Two radial joint lines divide the ring into two semicircular bodies, one joint at the left of the ring and one at the right of the ring. The upper semicircular body is the first frame half 10 and the lower semicircular body is the second frame half 12.

At the left joint is the hinge 14, drawn schematically as a small circle centred on that joint line with a short knuckle block reaching to it from each frame end.

At the right joint is the latch 16, drawn schematically as a rectangular block lying outside the outer boundary of the ring and bridging both frame ends, with an elongated lever extending from the block alongside the outer boundary of the second frame half 12.

Three jaw carriages 30 are spaced around the ring, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right. Each is drawn as a block that crosses the inner boundary of the ring and reaches radially inward toward the pipe 90. The topmost jaw carriage lies on the first frame half 10; the other two lie on the second frame half 12.

Each jaw carriage 30 carries at its inner end a separate member, joined to the jaw carriage 30 at a small circle that is a pivot shown schematically. The inner face of that member is a shallow concave arc that meets the outer surface of the pipe 90. That member is the jaw pad 40.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 100 split pipe clamp: target the outer boundary of the ring in the upper right region.
- 10 first frame half: target well inside the upper semicircular body, between its boundaries, right of the topmost jaw carriage.
- 12 second frame half: target well inside the lower semicircular body, between its boundaries, at the bottom of the ring.
- 14 hinge: target the small circle at the left joint.
- 16 latch: target the rectangular block bridging the right joint.
- 30 jaw carriage: target well inside the block of the topmost jaw carriage.
- 40 jaw pad: target well inside the member at the inner end of the topmost jaw carriage.
- 90 pipe: target well inside the central circle.

# FIG. 2

## View
Plan view of the segmented cam ring alone, removed from the frame, its two segments coupled, viewed along the axis of the ring. Black line work on white, no shading, all of it well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
A flat annulus at the centre of the drawing area, bounded by an inner circular boundary and an outer circular boundary, is the segmented cam ring 20. The space inside the inner boundary is empty.

Two joints, one at the left and one at the right, divide the annulus into two arcuate segments. The upper segment is the first cam ring segment 22 and the lower segment is the second cam ring segment 24.

At the left joint the two segment ends meet along plain complementary surfaces that face circumferentially, one surface on the end of the first cam ring segment 22 and one on the end of the second cam ring segment 24. Those surfaces are the complementary coupling faces at the hinge end 26.

At the right joint the two segment ends meet in the same way, along plain complementary surfaces that face circumferentially. Those surfaces are the complementary coupling faces at the latch end 28.

Three elongated openings pass through the annulus, one near the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, spaced from one another and from both joints. Each is an oblique slot 34, drawn as a long narrow opening with rounded ends, lying within the width of the annulus and clearly inclined to the radius at its own position, so that one end of the slot is nearer the inner boundary and the other nearer the outer boundary. All three are inclined alike.

Near the right joint, the outer boundary of the second cam ring segment 24 runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants inward as it approaches that joint, so that the segment is shallower at the joint than a short distance away from it. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the outer boundary of the annulus in the upper right region.
- 22 first cam ring segment: target well inside the upper segment, in its upper left region.
- 24 second cam ring segment: target well inside the lower segment, at the bottom of the annulus.
- 26 complementary coupling faces at the hinge end: target the meeting surfaces at the left joint.
- 28 complementary coupling faces at the latch end: target the meeting surfaces at the right joint.
- 34 oblique slot: target well inside the opening near the top of the annulus.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the outer boundary near the right joint.

# FIG. 3

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section through one jaw carriage, the cutting plane containing that carriage's radial direction and the frame axis. Radially outward is toward the top; the axis direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships

# FIG. 4

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section of the latch, viewed as in FIG. 1, so that radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area.

## Geometry and relationships
At the lower left a plain hatched body in section carries the parts shown. A shallow open channel in its upper face holds a hatched arcuate band running from the left edge of the view toward the middle. That band is the segmented cam ring 20. Near the right end of the band, its upper side runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants downward toward the right. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

To the right, a hatched enclosure in section stands on the plain body, with a left wall, a right wall and a top wall around a cavity that opens downward above the right end of the band. That enclosure is the latch housing 58.

A block lies in the lower part of the cavity between the left and right walls, which guide it up and down. Its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears against it, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52.

Above that block, a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line running from the upper face of the wedge 52 up to a flat plate lying across the cavity. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54.

An elongated lever is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle in the upper right of the cavity and extends upward and to the right, passing out above the right wall and ending well inside the drawing area. A short link joins the lever to the flat plate, so the lever presses the plate downward. The lever leans right, past the upright, in the over-centre position. That lever is the latch handle 50.

A slender pin rises from the flat plate, passes through a hole in the top wall of the latch housing 58 and stands above it. That pin is the indicator pin 56.

## Numerals on this sheet
- 16 latch: target the outer boundary of the enclosure at its lower right corner.
- 20 segmented cam ring: target the hatching of the arcuate band, near the left of the view.
- 36 ring drive face: target the slanting surface on the upper side of the band.
- 50 latch handle: target well inside the lever, above the top wall.
- 52 wedge: target well inside the block in the lower part of the cavity.
- 54 force-limiting spring stack: target the zigzag line above that block.
- 56 indicator pin: target the part of the pin standing above the top wall.
- 58 latch housing: target well inside the hatching of the top wall of the enclosure.

# FIG. 4

## View
Enlarged fragmentary section of the latch, viewed as in FIG. 1, so that radially outward is toward the top and the circumferential direction runs left to right. Cut solid material carries section hatching; black line work on white, well inside the drawing area. The flat plate is a spring seat shown schematically.

## Geometry and relationships
At the lower left a plain hatched body in section carries the parts shown. A shallow open channel in its upper face holds a hatched arcuate band running from the left edge of the view toward the middle. That band is the segmented cam ring 20. Near the right end of the band, its upper side runs for a short distance as a straight surface that slants downward toward the right. That slanting surface is the ring drive face 36.

To the right, a hatched enclosure in section stands on the plain body, with a left wall, a right wall and a top wall around a cavity that opens downward above the right end of the band. That enclosure is the latch housing 58.

A block lies in the lower part of the cavity between the left and right walls, which guide it up and down. Its lower left face slants at the same angle as the ring drive face 36 and bears against it, so that downward movement of the block drives the band to the left. That block is the wedge 52.

Above that block, a compression spring is drawn as a zigzag line running from the upper face of the wedge 52 up to a flat plate lying across the cavity. That spring is the force-limiting spring stack 54.

An elongated lever is pivoted to the latch housing 58 at a small circle in the upper right of the cavity and extends upward and to the right, passing out above the right wall and ending well inside the drawing area. The lever bears directly on the flat plate and presses it downward. The lever leans right, past the upright, in the over-centre position. That lever is the latch handle 50.

A slender pin rises from the flat plate, passes through a hole in the top wall of the latch housing 58 and stands above it. That pin is the indicator pin 56.

The first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 meet at two places, one at the hinge end and one at the latch end. At the hinge end the two segments have complementary coupling faces 26, and at the latch end they have complementary coupling faces 28. The complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 are circumferentially facing drive faces, each pair being shaped so that one segment can transmit circumferential force to the other through the joint. The faces are brought into engagement by the same motion that closes the frame halves: as the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 are swung together about the hinge 14 and the latch 16 is engaged, the complementary coupling faces 26 close on one another at the hinge end and the complementary coupling faces 28 close on one another at the latch end.

Coupling the segments in this way solves a problem created by splitting the clamp. A clamp that must open from the side cannot carry a continuous drive ring across the split, and a divided drive must otherwise be operated separately in each half, with the result that the two halves advance their jaws by amounts that are not fixed relative to one another. Here the division of the ring is undone by the act of closing the clamp. In the closed condition the first cam ring segment 22 and the second cam ring segment 24 are coupled at both ends and rotate together in the annular guide as a coupled ring, and a circumferential input applied to either segment is carried around the whole ring. One input, applied at one point on one frame half, therefore reaches every jaw carriage 30 through a single kinematic element, and the relationship between the jaw carriages 30 is set by the geometry of the ring rather than by the way the clamp is operated. When the latch 16 is released and the frame halves are swung apart, the complementary coupling faces 26 and the complementary coupling faces 28 separate and each segment stays with its own frame half, so that the coupling is made and broken by the closing and opening of the frame halves.

The segmented cam ring 20 has three oblique slots 34, one for each jaw carriage 30. Each oblique slot 34 passes through the segmented cam ring 20 and is inclined to the radial direction of the frame at the circumferential position of that slot, so that circumferential movement of the ring produces a radial displacement of anything constrained to follow the slot. Each oblique slot 34 is inclined so that rotation of the coupled ring produces inward travel of its jaw carriage 30, the three oblique slots 34 being arranged so that the three jaw carriages 30 travel inwardly in synchronism. The inclination of the oblique slots 34 sets the ratio between the circumferential stroke of the coupled ring and the radial travel of the jaw carriages 30.

The segmented cam ring 20 further has a ring drive face 36, shown in FIG. 2 at the latch end of the ring, against which the latch acts as described below. The ring drive face 36 is presented at a position on the ring that the wedge of the latch can reach, in the illustrated embodiment on the segment adjacent the latch end, and it lies at an inclination to the direction in which that wedge advances, so that advance of the wedge moves the segmented cam ring 20 circumferentially.
The follower 32 is constrained in two ways at once. The radial guide 38 prevents the jaw carriage 30, and therefore the follower 32, from moving circumferentially, while the oblique slot 34 confines the follower 32 to a path that is inclined to the radial direction. When the coupled ring turns through its stroke, the side of each oblique slot 34 bears on the corresponding follower 32 and drives it, and with it the jaw carriage 30, radially inward along the radial guide 38. Because all three followers 32 are engaged in oblique slots 34 of one coupled ring, the three jaw carriages 30 advance inwardly in synchronism for as long as the ring turns. The jaw pads therefore close on the pipe together.

At its inner end each jaw carriage 30 carries a jaw pad 40. The jaw pad 40 is pivotally mounted on the jaw carriage 30 and has a concave bearing face directed inwardly of the frame. Because the jaw pad 40 is free to pivot on the jaw carriage 30, the concave bearing face aligns itself with the outer surface of the pipe as it lands. The same concave bearing face therefore seats on pipes of different diameters, and no insert dimensioned to a particular pipe diameter is required.

A carriage return spring 44 acts between each jaw carriage 30 and the frame so as to urge that jaw carriage 30 radially outward. When the latch 16 is released and the drive from the latch to the ring drive face 36 is removed, the carriage return springs 44 push the jaw carriages 30 outward and the jaw pads 40 are retracted from the pipe, and the clamp 100 is left with its jaw carriages 30 retracted and ready for the next installation. Retraction of the jaw carriages 30 clears the jaw pads 40 from the pipe before the frame halves are swung apart.

The latch and the force-limiting drive train

FIG. 4 shows the latch 16 in fragmentary section. The latch 16 includes a latch housing 58 mounted on the frame at the latch end, a latch handle 50 pivotally mounted on the latch housing 58, a wedge 52 movable in the latch housing 58, and a force-limiting spring stack 54 in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52. The wedge 52 is positioned so that its inclined face bears on the ring drive face 36 of the segmented cam ring 20.

The latch 16 has two engaged positions. In a first position, the latch 16 holds the first frame half 10 and the second frame half 12 closed around the pipe 90 but does not clamp it: the frame is captive on the pipe 90 and cannot fall away, while the jaw carriages 30 remain retracted under their carriage return springs 44. In a second, over-center position, the wedge 52 drives the segmented cam ring 20 and the pipe 90 is clamped. Movement of the latch handle 50 from the first position to the second position advances the wedge 52 against the ring drive face 36. The inclined face of the wedge 52 converts that advance into circumferential movement of the segmented cam ring 20, and the coupled ring turns through its limited stroke, the extent of the stroke being set by the travel of the wedge 52 between the first and second positions of the latch 16.

The force-limiting spring stack 54 answers the problem of what becomes of the operator's remaining handle travel. The jaw pads 40 land on the pipe 90 at some point in the stroke that depends on the diameter of the pipe 90, and the latch handle 50 has still to be carried into its over-center position. If the drive train from the latch handle 50 to the wedge 52 were rigid, that remaining travel would be taken up by whatever part of the assembly yielded first, in practice by driving one jaw farther into the pipe 90 than the others and loading it far more heavily. Additional travel of the latch handle 50 after all three jaw pads 40 have contacted the pipe 90 compresses the force-limiting spring stack 54 rather than forcing one jaw carriage 30 farther inward than the others.

An indicator pin 56 is coupled to the force-limiting spring stack 54 and projects from the latch housing 58. As the force-limiting spring stack 54 compresses, the indicator pin 56 moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing 58, and the position of the indicator pin 56 with respect to that fixed edge shows the operator when the force-limiting spring stack 54 has entered a predetermined compression range. The predetermined compression range is the range of stack compression that corresponds to the clamping force for which the clamp 100 is intended. The indicator pin 56 therefore reports clamp loading mechanically, at the clamp itself and without any separate instrument, and what it reports is the state of the force-limiting spring stack 54. It is not a measurement of the diameter of the pipe 90.

Operation
Variations

The force-limiting spring stack 54 lies in the drive train between the latch handle 50 and the wedge 52.

Features described above in connection with one embodiment may be combined with features described in connection with another, except where the context makes the combination impossible. The embodiments described are illustrative of the disclosed clamp and are not exhaustive of it, and the scope of protection is defined by the claims that follow rather than by any particular embodiment described here.

The current draft did not pass the automatic filing gate.

Read review/previous-qa.md, then fix every listed mechanical check and every independently
verified finding. Do not argue with a finding in the structured response. If wording triggered a
false positive, make the draft unambiguous enough that the check passes without changing the
invention. Keep the reference-numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims,
and every file in figures/ synchronized.

Generated pixels are never authority for the invention. The authority order is the inventor's
disclosure and conversation, then the patent text, then the figure briefs, then the rendered
sheets. Never change the claims, description, numeral table, or disclosed embodiments merely to
excuse geometry, an object, or a leader endpoint that the image model drew incorrectly. Never add
an implementation detail or embodiment because it appeared in a generated image. For a drawing
finding, preserve the authoritative invention, strengthen the figure brief, and regenerate the
sheet from the authoritative text until the pixels conform. A stubborn rendering artifact remains
a drawing defect; it does not become part of the invention.

For a figure-plan coverage failure, never delete a disclosed part, numeral definition, or
supporting specification text. Redistribute labels among focused sheets, or add a focused sheet
when necessary, and synchronize the drawing descriptions.

If a figure brief is over-specified, shorten it by removing invented rendering constraints while
preserving the authoritative text, numeral table, disclosed geometry, and required relationships.
Replace generic negative linework controls with positive descriptions of the required bodies,
edges, contacts, openings, and paths. Do not ban second boundaries, parallel lines, inner lines,
rims, ledges, or chamfers merely to suppress a prior rendering artifact.
Remove generic face-linework controls such as prescribing one stroke for every outline or a
shared edge drawn once. Keep only the positive physical geometry and relationship.
For an endpoint finding, choose a broad interior target on the intended part whenever possible.
Remove exact midpoint, depth, quarter, or toward-an-end modifiers that are not disclosure-grounded
or necessary to distinguish the intended part. Replace ordinal geometry references with explicit
outermost, middle, innermost, left, or right terms whenever the order could be read in more than
one direction.

Leave no note, placeholder, question, or instruction for a person. Return the structured answer
with `action` set to "revised" and `questions` as an empty array.
